rules.rule: Numbers round half up (0.5 becomes 1). They are never cut off.
Damage is worked out in decimals and rounded once, at the very end. One hit is capped at 9,999,999. Stats are capped at 9,999,999 too.
In-game max HP and max shield are 85% of the raw base value, then the extra % from job, race or gear effects is applied. Max HP is never below 1.
HP stacks are NOT scaled by 0.85. The race Hive gets +1 max HP stack from its own race effect.
The three apparent exceptions to the 0.85 rule are job effects: Ancientmancer +30% max shield, Jester +25% max shield, Eccentricity +25% max HP.
Starting stat at Lv 1 = race + job + origin + equipped gear.
A stat = base + flat bonuses - flat penalties (if that is 0 or less it becomes 0). Then the percent-up bonuses add together and are applied, and percent-down reductions are applied afterwards.
Several "%+" modifiers on the SAME stat multiply each other. An "=" modifier overwrites earlier values. A "Force" modifier ends the chain.
Modifiers are probably applied in a fixed order, but that order is not known for certain.

Skills read the four main stats as STR, DEX, INT, PIE (stat 1 to 4). Base damage = stat x skill power%. A skill that lists several stats ADDS them; a skill with alternatives ("/") uses the HIGHEST one.
A skill's "bonus from a stat" is a percent bonus on its power. It is not extra power per use.
A hit happens when a random roll comes in below the hit chance.

Normal hit chance = skill hit rate + your Accu + skill accuracy bonus + target Avoid-penalty - your Accu-penalty - target Avoid - skill accuracy penalty; then the "hitting" / "being hit" percent modifiers; then limited to 5..95.

Always-hit effects (Surehit, no-avoid, Sniper) give 100. Always-miss effects and the Blind rune give 0. The Rough Aim rune gives 50. A "last-hit" effect only hits if the previous effect hit. An effect with no avoid type uses its own hit rate.
Ailment hit chance = skill value + your Effective - target Resist Ailment (and the ailment's own Effective / Resist when one specific ailment is applied); then modifiers; then limited to 5..95.

Crit chance = (your Crit Rate + skill crit bonus) x the skill's own crit multiplier, then the crit modifiers, minus target Avoid Crit and skill crit penalty, then the "taking crit" modifiers, then limited to 5..95.

Absolute-crit effects force 100. An attacker with a no-crit effect, or a target with a no-take-crit effect, forces 0. Crit runes: weak / mid / strong add +10 / +15 / +25 crit chance; extreme = guaranteed crit.
Whether an attack can crit at all depends on the skill (many attacks can) or on a state that grants it. Heals cannot crit.

rules.topic: Damage chain (order of one damage number)
rules.rule: 1) base power plus the stat percent bonus. 2) a long list of percent modifiers, each MULTIPLYING the next: skill power, damage type, target type, elite targets, direct / indirect, burst / non-burst skill, low base accuracy, HP-rate effects and others. 3) source bonuses (below). 4) crit. 5) armor. 6) element/type handling. 7) damage-dealt / damage-taken modifiers. 8) Persistence cap. 9) parry. 10) final clamp 0..9,999,999.

rules.topic: Damage chain (order of one damage number)
rules.rule: Damage-over-time, delayed, reflect and pursuit damage each get their own bonus from the attacker. It multiplies, never adds. Every step is value x (100 + n)/100.

rules.topic: Damage chain (order of one damage number)
rules.rule: Burn, Frostbite and Electric bonuses partly carry over to each other: the other two count at a percentage set by the cross-element stat (rounded half up).

rules.topic: Damage chain (order of one damage number)
rules.rule: For physical, magic and void direct damage: if the TARGET carries one of Bleed, Burn, Poison, Explode, Frostbite or Hex, damage is multiplied by the attacker's direct-damage bonus for that ailment. The six multiply.

rules.topic: Damage chain (order of one damage number)
rules.rule: A crit multiplies damage by 1.5, then crit-damage modifiers apply on top.
Damage has three types: physical (P), magic (M), void (V), each with its own armor.
Armor is a percent cut, limited to 75. States that raise the armor cap (Iron wall, Sanctuary, Mutation) lift the limit to 95. Negative armor ADDS damage.
A crit ignores POSITIVE armor. Penetrate runes (P / M / V) ignore armor of that type. Penetration is subtracted from the target's armor.
Damage can be converted physical -> magic -> void by a percent (conversion effects and the Enchant / Eldritch runes). Each part is then cut by its own armor.

Damage-over-time (Bleed, Burn, Poison, Doomsday Flame), delayed (Explode, Frostbite, Hex), reflect (Electric, Karma, Revenge, Thorn) and pursuit (Erosion, Hidden Blade, Spell Bullet) damage can also be cut by a matching source armor, limited to 75 (it does not use the 95 limit). It multiplies with normal armor.
Several named state attacks also use an armor tied to that attack.
Parry chance = the attacker's "target parry" modifiers applied over (the target's parry modifiers applied over the target's Parry stat), limited to 0..95.

A parry only happens on direct attacks (damage becomes 0, "Parry!" shows). Against status effects only DEBUFFS can be parried, never buffs. Several effects cannot be parried (Stone Bind, Slow, Entangle Root, Storm Bind and others). Some effects make nobody able to parry.
Parry sources: shields and the parry gear effect (15 per gear rarity), warrior and shield-bearer enemy types (15), elite shield (25), a few runes and skills.

rules.topic: Applying damage, death, HP stacks, Guts
rules.rule: Damage hits the shield first, then HP. A miss shows a miss popup and deals nothing.

rules.topic: Applying damage, death, HP stacks, Guts
rules.rule: A unit starts every fight at full HP, full shield and full HP stacks. The "dying" flag is never set in normal play.

rules.topic: Applying damage, death, HP stacks, Guts
rules.rule: A unit is alive while it has an ignore-death effect, or HP above 0, or at least 1 HP stack. A unit is also dead when the total remaining uses of all its non-free skills is below 1.

rules.topic: Applying damage, death, HP stacks, Guts
rules.rule: Spending an HP stack (needs a hit and HP at 0): a Guts roll keeps the stack; otherwise one stack is spent. Either way HP is refilled to max.

rules.topic: Applying damage, death, HP stacks, Guts
rules.rule: WHEN the stack is spent: only at the start of that unit's own turn (both units are checked each turn start) and at battle end. So a unit at 0 HP with stacks stays alive until its own next turn start.

rules.topic: Applying damage, death, HP stacks, Guts
rules.rule: Guts chance = the Guts stat limited to 0..95 (so a stack is never 100% safe), roll random 0-99 below it. Guts sources: gear (15 to 30), a few states, one enemy type, elites.

rules.topic: Applying damage, death, HP stacks, Guts
rules.rule: "Lose HP stack" effects: no hit / dead target / no stacks = nothing. Otherwise a Guts roll can save the stack ("Guts!"); on failure the stacks drop by the effect value (not below 0). Only the stack count changes: no HP or shield change, no refill.

rules.topic: Applying damage, death, HP stacks, Guts
rules.rule: "Gain HP stack" effects: need a hit, a living target and non-full stacks. They add the effect value, capped at max stacks. "Reset HP stack" sets stacks to the maximum (Camp, a gear effect, Call Miracle).

rules.topic: Applying damage, death, HP stacks, Guts
rules.rule: The Devil race sets HP and stacks to 0 when it loses a soulstone; probably this kills it at 0 soulstones.
Turn order is NOT speed. After every turn the other side acts, so the sides alternate.
The player usually acts first; the enemy opens a fight about 1 time in 3.
A follower acts instead of its owner when the owner has one.

Quick actions (extra action, "+1 Action!"): free skills are never quick; a No-Quick state on the unit blocks it; otherwise quick comes from a skill's own quick flag, forced-quick effects, or a chance from "add action" effects.
A quick action probably lets the same side act again.
The enemy picks among its usable skills (not on cooldown, and uses left or free).
Some "Prior:" runes (for example Away and Force) make the enemy favour or avoid certain skills. An enemy with no such runes picks UNIFORMLY at random among its usable skills.
A confused player's skill is chosen by the same rule. Uncontrollable comes from Confuse, the Automaton race and the Werewolf race; Mentality makes you immune.

Each enemy drop names ONE exact item and has a drop chance out of 10,000 (100 = 1%). The drop happens when a random number from 0 to 9999 is below round(drop chance x rate/100); the base rate is 100. Only one reward per enemy.

The Capture state on an enemy at the win raises the chance of that enemy's capture item from 1% to 10% (drop chance 100 -> 1000 out of 10,000). Main drops are unchanged. Capture comes from the Spider Snare burst, the Scholar job's Arresting (on crit) and Capture runes. Whether the state is still on the enemy at the win is unproven.
Rarity rolls for skill / rune / gear picks use the run Progress, and Risk (100 or more = risk mode). The upper limit is 5 (7 in risk mode). Rarity 6 and 7 need risk mode (Savage).
Reroll power N gives N extra tries for +1 star. Sources: the enhanced-reroll state, three origins, and buying a shop reroll contract (levels 1 / 3 / 5 / 7), which overwrites it.
The enhanced-reroll state comes only from a random tier-4 gear effect. Its odds are unknown.

High-rarity camp items are picked WEIGHTED (some items are more likely than others) within the current dungeon. High-rarity gear and skills are picked UNIFORMLY among the dungeon items with the rolled rarity (gear also by slot).
Rarity below 5 camp items come from the whole camp item list (weighted).
Pick screens can require a minimum rarity (set by the effect that made them).
Items have real-calendar availability windows; an item outside its window cannot drop.
Dropped gear is built at the PLAYER'S level with the item's rarity. Higher rarity means more effects, up to 5 in total. Basic rarity-1 gear has 2 fixed and 0 random effects.
A rolled rarity 2 / 3 / 4 picks a basic piece with 3 / 4 / 5 effects (2 fixed + 1 / 2 / 3 random). Rarity 5 picks a unique piece of the same slot.
Some basic pieces only appear after a run Progress threshold.
Rerolling gear: rarity +1, or 25% add a parameter, or a fresh roll.
Enemies have type tags that give permanent effects.
Elite modifiers are percents on HP, shield, main stats, HP stacks, score, soulstones and exp. Rewards scale by the same percent.
Every skill has 1 to 4 modes (mode 1 normal; mode 2 is probably Brave). A mode has uses, cooldown, quick flag and damage types.
Enemy skills can be set to never Burst or always Burst.
A state lasts for a number of acts, turns, combats, rooms or floors.
State triggers: chance = base chance x (linked state value)/100, roll random 0-99 below it. The unit must carry the state and pass the condition.
